svg.title: Azure Local VM scenarios
svg.desc: Azure Local guest VM Arc connectivity. Outbound proxy means a customer-configured forward proxy, not the Arc proxy inside a guest. Guest applications have their own customer-controlled proxy and bypass settings. Arc-enabled guests do not use the host cluster IP proxy or host Arc tunnel. Enabling a gateway does not automatically proxy arbitrary guest application traffic. Packet motion is continuous and illustrative; reduced-motion preferences hide moving packets. The outbound proxy and Arc gateway are independent choices. The firewall represents network transit, not TLS inspection. The detailed views illustrate forwarding responsibilities, not a prescribed ExpressRoute, VPN, NAT, or internet topology. Every configuration still requires a permitted route to its public endpoints. With Arc gateway enabled, each guest uses its own Arc proxy and tunnel, even if the Azure gateway resource is shared. The four quadrants are alternative configurations, not concurrent paths for one VM. The top row has no outbound proxy and the bottom row has a proxy. Arc gateway is off in the left column and on in the right column. Muted components are not used by that route. Firewall transit, network transport, and additional endpoint exceptions are omitted from this logical comparison, not bypassed. Each detailed scenario shows those distinctions.
svg.text: Guest Arc connectivity / four independent configurations

path.title: Direct guest Arc connectivity without an outbound proxy, guest Arc proxy, or Arc gateway hop. Firewall and network transit are still required.

The guest Arc agent uses the Arc proxy inside this VM.
